Header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Maria Lopez (SummitPay - Head of ML), Samir Patel (SummitPay - Infra), Priya Rao (SummitPay - CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and KV/prefix cache cost model; baseline numbers, sample prompt profile, and POC next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll give folks another minute but welcome, i'm alex from redwood, AE on this account.
[00:08] Maria Lopez: thanks alex, and hi jordan - excited to see the optimize stuff, we've been seeing token costs creep up.
[00:12] Jordan Park: yeah hi team, i'm jordan, performance eng, i'm gonna run through a couple slides and then walk the cost model with you.
[00:19] Priya Rao: thanks, high level we care about 95th percentile latency under 300ms for chat completions, and keeping monthly cost under our internal threshold.
[00:28] Alex Chen: got it - we'll purposely focus on tradeoffs: batching increases throughput/cost efficiency but can add latency, whereas prefix/KV caching saves tokens for repeated contexts, big wins for your flows if you have heavy session reuse.
[00:40] Samir Patel: quick question, are we talking hosted API or dedicated nodes? our infra team prefers dedicated for PCI.
[00:46] Jordan Park: good callout, for this walkthrough i'l cover both - the cost model will show hosted vs dedicated delta; recommended path for pci is private/dedicated.
[00:54] Alex Chen: okay i'll share the spreadsheet after - 00:55 jordan, take it away.

[01:05] Jordan Park: slide 1, objectives - reduce per-token cost 20-60% depending on workload, preserve tail latency SLOs. slide 2, baseline: we measured your sample trace (maria's set) - average prompt length ~120 tokens, average completion 60 tokens, 3k qps during peak bursts.
[01:25] Maria Lopez: that prompt length sounds right, though the completion varies - some flows are 400 tokens.
[01:29] Jordan Park: noted, I used distribution from top 10% of calls to estimate tail.
[01:35] [01:36] Jordan Park: batching overview - continuous batching in the runtime will aggregate concurrent requests into micro-batches at millisecond granularity. for high qps endpoints we recommend target batch windows of 5-20ms to get high GPU utilization and keep P95 in your 300ms SLO.
[01:51] Alex Chen: a note - batching policy is workload-aware, we can autosize windows or pin to fixed window; autosize tries to balance latency and throughput.
[01:58] Samir Patel: what's the impact if traffic is bursty? we have sudden skews from marketing campaigns.
[02:03] Jordan Park: bursts actually help batching, more concurrent requests -> better batching efficiency. the risk is low baseline traffic where batching can add waiting time; that's where adaptive windows or prefilling strategies help.

[02:20] Jordan Park: next, prefix/KV cache - two patterns we saw in your prompts: 1) long shared system prompt and 2) per-session repeated user context (e.g., last 3 turns). caching the prefix embeddings and KV cache can avoid re-sending and re-computing up to ~70% of tokens for session-based flows.
[02:40] Maria Lopez: does that mean we can reduce tokens billed, or is it compute-level only?
[02:44] Alex Chen: both - token billing depends on provider; with redwood hosted we meter per-input tokens but Optimize recommends keeping prompts smaller and using KV cache to avoid re-generation; in Dedicated/Private the runtime reduces compute cycles which maps to lower infra cost.
[02:58] Priya Rao: any gotchas with cache invalidation - e.g., if the system prompt changes or we do model rollouts?
[03:04] Jordan Park: yes cache invalidation is important - we recommend tagging cache entries with model version and session id; on rollout you purge or keep dual caches for canary ratio. we walked this in the notes - i'll share the doc.

[03:20] [03:21] Jordan Park: cost model walk - here's a simplified equation in the sheet: effective_token_cost = (raw_token_cost * (1 - cache_hit_rate)) / batching_efficiency. so if you have 50% cache hit and batching_efficiency 1.8x, you get big savings.
[03:40] Alex Chen: for summitpay numbers we plugged in: raw per-token $0.0008 hosted baseline (example), projected cache hit 40% conservative, batching eff 1.5x -> ~46% cost reduction in the compute component.
[03:54] Samir Patel: that hosted token price seems optimistic compared to public pricing - is that Redwood list or includes model licensing?
[04:00] Alex Chen: it's illustrative; we'll replace with your actual model costs in the spreadsheet. for dedicated nodes, cost per token shifts to infra amortized across throughput - the sheet models both.

[04:12] Maria Lopez: can we see a concrete example with our highest-traffic flow?
[04:16] Jordan Park: yes, i took the sample prompt set you shared last week; i'll show three scenarios: no cache/no batching, batching only, batching + KV cache.
[04:25] [04:26] Jordan Park: Scenario A (no cache/no batching): avg latency 210ms, throughput 2k qps, token cost X. Scenario B (batching only): avg latency 240ms, throughput 3.6k qps, token cost -33%. Scenario C (batching + KV prefix cache): avg latency 230ms, throughput 3.5k qps, token cost -55%.
[04:45] Priya Rao: interesting that latency for scenario C improves vs B slightly, isn't cache hit adding CPU overhead?
[04:51] Jordan Park: cache lookup is cheap compared to full decode; plus fewer tokens to decode reduces decode time on the GPU. decoding is typically the hotspot.

[05:05] Samir Patel: any extra storage costs or operational complexity for the KV cache? our infra team worries about stateful components.
[05:11] Alex Chen: good question - on hosted we manage the cache; on dedicated/private we offer an optional managed cache service or you can bring-your-own redis/raft store. the spreadsheet models a small storage + IOPS cost, usually under 2-5% of your monthly bill but varies by retention window.
[05:29] Maria Lopez: retention window - how long do you keep session KV? we want to keep last 24 hours for fraud detection flows.
[05:35] Jordan Park: configurable - sliding window TTL, plus eviction by size. for 24h retention and your qps, rough estimate 120GB of KV storage - again I'll add numbers to the sheet.

[05:50] [05:51] Jordan Park: tradeoffs checklist:
- If strict P95 latency is primary: smaller batch windows, more conservative batching; you still get some efficiency but less than peak.
- If cost is primary: larger windows, aggressive batching, and longer KV retention for prefix sharing.
- If data residency/SOC2 required: prefer dedicated/private and host KV in your VPC.

[06:18] Priya Rao: security: how do we handle encryption and KMS for KV cache?
[06:22] Alex Chen: for private/dedicated we integrate with your KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and SOC2 controls, plus audit logs for cache access. i'll attach SOC2 summary.

[06:36] Maria Lopez: can we run a quick sensitivity analysis live? like change cache hit from 30 to 60%?
[06:40] Jordan Park: yep - I have the sheet open - changing hit rate to 60% shows compute component down another 20% and overall token-equivalent cost drops by ~12 points.
[06:53] [06:54] Jordan Park: note on rollouts: when you change system prompt we recommend key rotation pattern: create new model tag + new cache namespace, warm the cache with canary traffic then ramp. that avoids invalidating everything abruptly.

[07:15] Samir Patel: operational question - network egress for KV store if hosted vs in-vpc? latency implications?
[07:22] Jordan Park: yes if the KV store is remote you add ms; we recommend colocated cache within same AZ or VPC peering to keep lookup sub-ms. hosted default is colocated in our infra.

[07:35] Alex Chen: quick interruption - competition, sometimes customers ask about Anthropic or OpenAI managed endpoints - main differentiator here is that Redwood Optimize gives you explicit levers to trade cost vs latency and integrate KV caching with rollout controls.
[07:49] Maria Lopez: got it, we evaluate on cost curves not just raw accuracy.

[07:55] Jordan Park: a couple more practical things - instrumentation: we'll surface token-level cost and latency per route in console, you can set alerts when effective cost per request goes above threshold, and Optimize can suggest batching window tweaks.
[08:09] Maria Lopez: can you trigger automatic policy changes based on SLO violations?
[08:12] Jordan Park: currently we support suggestions and automated canary-based rollouts; fully automated SLO-driven policy is roadmap but we can implement guardrails via alerts and scriptable webhooks.

[08:26] [08:27] Alex Chen: ok we're about halfway through, any big questions we should prioritize before the POC?
[08:33] Priya Rao: licensing for models - if we use open weights with quantization on dedicated, what's the experience?
[08:39] Jordan Park: we support quantized execution paths; for licensed models you need to adhere to the model license, and Redwood runtime will pick quant kernels accordingly. cost model includes perf deltas for quantized runs.

[08:55] Maria Lopez: are there any accuracy/regression risks when we do caching and batching? sometimes shorter contexts change model output.
[09:01] Jordan Park: yes, caching can change context length and inference path; we recommend an eval set to compare outputs before/after and monitor quality metrics. Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets so we'll alert on drift.

[09:18] Samir Patel: how long does it take to get a POC environment up? we have a compliance window next month.
[09:23] Alex Chen: for a scoped POC focused on batching+KV, we can provision dedicated test capacity in ~2 weeks, or a hosted sandbox in a couple days. timeline depends on security review for dedicated.

[09:36] Jordan Park: ok demo of the console quickly - showing per-route token cost, batching histogram, and cache hit heatmap (link: https://console.redwood.ai/demo/summitpay-optimize) - note the heatmap shows peak daytime cache hits ~45% for this route.
[09:55] Maria Lopez: that heatmap is helpful. can we annotate by user cohort?
[09:58] Jordan Park: yes we can tag routes and filter by cohort; the console supports segmentation.

[10:06] [10:07] Alex Chen: closing - recap of next steps: we will share the cost model sheet with scenario calculations, security/SOC2 summary, and sample POC runbook. also schedule scoping session.
[10:20] Priya Rao: perfect, please include estimate for KV storage and op costs.
[10:23] Maria Lopez: i'll follow up with the full prompt set and traffic profile.
[10:27] Alex Chen: awesome, thanks all. we'll send notes and the sheet by EOD tomorrow.
[10:33] Jordan Park: thanks everyone, speak soon.
[10:36] [10:37] Meeting end
